note: Hablar → hablo with yo. You can also say Hablo español; the verb identifies the subject.
Tú is informal singular you. Hablas is present tense; muy claro means very clearly. Use usted habla for formal address.
Regular -ar verbs use -a with él or ella. Él means he; el without an accent means the.
Ella takes estudia. Por la noche means at night.
Vivir → vivimos with nosotros or nosotras. The subject pronoun is often omitted.
Comer → comen with ellos. For an all-female group, use ellas comen juntas.
In Latin America, ustedes is the usual plural you and takes the same verb form as ellos.

en: Could you help me for a moment, please?
note: Ayuda is the present usted form of ayudar. A question plus por favor makes a courteous request.
Entender changes e → ie in entiendo. Put no before the verb to make it negative.
Querer changes e → ie in quieres. A question can keep the same word order as a statement.
Tener que + infinitive expresses an obligation: tengo que salir = I have to leave.
Poder is followed by an infinitive. The nosotros form podemos keeps o, unlike puedo.
Use saber for knowing a fact or an answer.
Use conocer for knowing a person. The personal a comes before tu hermano.
Use estar for someone's location. Estoy is its yo form.
Use ser de to state where someone is from.
Spanish uses tener hambre, literally to have hunger. Tener → tenemos with we.
Use tener frío to describe feeling cold. Tienes addresses one person informally.
Hace calor describes hot weather. Hoy can go at the beginning or the end.
Hay means there is or there are; it stays the same with one thing or several.
With gustar, the song is the grammatical subject: me gusta + one thing.
Use gustan with plural things. Nos identifies us as the people who like them.
Levantarse uses a reflexive pronoun: me levanto for I get up.
Acostarse changes o → ue in se acuesta. Se goes before the conjugated verb.
Desayunar means to have breakfast. Desayunamos is the nosotros form.
The present tense can describe a routine. Cada mañana means every morning.

en: I go to work by bus.
note: Ir → voy with yo. A + el contracts to al; en autobús means by bus.
Venir → vienen with ustedes. Conmigo means with me.
Oír has the irregular yo form oigo.

en: Do you see that house? (one person)
note: Ver → ves with tú. Esa points to that feminine singular thing.
Poner has the irregular yo form pongo. Las llaves means the keys.
Decir → dice with él. Siempre commonly goes before the verb.

en: We do the shopping on Saturdays.
note: Hacer las compras means to do the shopping. Los sábados expresses a recurring Saturday routine.
Traer → trae with ella. Su can mean her, his, their, or your; context identifies the owner.
Pedir changes e → i in pido. La cuenta is the bill at a restaurant.
Dormir changes o → ue in duermen. Bien describes how they sleep.
Preferir changes e → ie in prefiero and can be followed by an infinitive.
Pensar changes e → ie in piensan. Lo mismo means the same thing.

es: La película empieza a las ocho.
note: Empezar changes e → ie in empieza. Use a las before most clock times.
Volver changes o → ue in vuelvo. A casa expresses movement toward home.
Estar + gerund describes an action in progress. Aprender → aprendiendo.
Buscar → buscando after estar. Buscar already means look for; no extra por is needed here.
Leer has the gerund leyendo. Ella está identifies the subject clearly.
Hacer → haciendo. Estás addresses tú, and qué introduces the question what.

en: I'm sorry, I don't have time right now.
es: Lo siento, no tengo tiempo ahora.
note: Lo siento politely softens the response. Tengo is the yo present form of tener.
The subject can follow the verb in a question. Ustedes makes plural you explicit.
Costar changes o → ue in cuesta. Use cuestan when asking about several things.
Spanish expresses age with tener + number + años, not with ser.
With doler, the body part is the subject. One head takes duele; me identifies whose pain it is.
Estar bien describes how things are. Todo takes the singular verb está.
